title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## µRepRap Micron-Scale 3D Printer

### The Breakthrough
The µRepRap project delivers an open‑source platform that achieves micron‑scale 3D printing using a RepRap‑style machine. By combining 400‑step NEMA17 motors, a custom Z‑touch probe and a capillary‑driven UV resin head, it reaches repeatable ~1 µm positioning and deposits resin droplets as small as 4 µm, enabling line widths down to 9 µm in an 8 mm³ workspace. This provides a concrete testbed for sub‑10 µm fabrication and flexure component development.

### The Caveats
The positioning claims rely on anecdotal measurements from the authors' prototype, with no systematic benchmark or comparison to existing micron‑fabrication systems.

## P³‑WAM Unified Manipulation Model

### The Breakthrough
P³‑WAM is a single model that learns 3D perception, action‑conditioned video prediction, and goal‑directed planning for egocentric dexterous manipulation. It embeds a compact 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer via a mixture‑of‑transformers architecture with shared weights and modality‑specific adapters, and uses randomized modality visibility to switch between perception, prediction, and planning modes. The unified training yields measurable gains on hand reconstruction, video prediction, and instruction‑following planning compared to single‑mode baselines.

### The Caveats
The paper does not name or compare against any existing baselines, leaving the reported performance improvements unsubstantiated.

## T2‑Z Test‑Time World Model Adaptation

### The Breakthrough
T2‑Z optimizes a compact environment latent at test time to adapt a frozen action‑conditioned dynamics model to new conditions. During training the method alternates between learning the dynamics model and optimizing per‑environment latents; at deployment a fresh latent is fitted from one or a few interaction trajectories, cutting prediction error from 15.20 to 7.00 and raising success rates from 33.73 % to 72.96 % across seven simulated scenarios and four real‑world robot tasks.

### The Caveats
No existing test‑time adaptation or latent‑based baselines are cited, so the relative advantage of T2‑Z is unclear.

## Value as Memory (VaM) Online Post‑Training

### The Breakthrough
VaM introduces value caching as a memory of recent task progress and combines offline demos, off‑policy interventions, and on‑policy rollouts in an online RL loop to improve generalist robot policies after deployment. Caching predicted values yields a 29.4 % absolute success‑rate boost, while the full online update adds another 32.8 % gain, delivering eight times more policy iterations and over twice the gradient‑step speed under the same compute budget.

### The Caveats
The study provides no ablation separating the impact of value‑caching from the online updates, so the source of the reported gains cannot be isolated.

## HUMXN Free Home Repairs Data Collection

### The Breakthrough
HUMXN offers free plumbing, HVAC, electrical, air‑duct and carpet cleaning services in three U.S. cities in exchange for wearable sensors that record video, pose, and tool usage of technicians. The platform captures diverse, climate‑related repair scenarios to build a large‑scale dataset of skilled‑trade motions for future robot training.

### The Caveats
The announcement includes no independent verification that the captured footage will enable functional robot skill learning, and no training results, benchmarks, or robot demonstrations are provided.

## LIBERO‑PeRM Preference Manipulation Benchmark

### The Breakthrough
LIBERO‑PeRM extends the LIBERO suite with a procedural pipeline that generates 312 simulated manipulation tasks annotated with language‑expressible user preferences and automatic satisfaction metrics. Experiments show vanilla VLA policies fail zero‑shot preference following, while supervised fine‑tuning and mixed training improve preference learning and retention.

### The Caveats
All results are confined to simulation; the benchmark provides no hardware experiments, so transfer to real robots remains uncertain.

## nano‑ros Rust ROS2 for Microcontrollers

### The Breakthrough
nano‑ros is a no‑std Rust library that lets bare‑metal microcontrollers and RTOS kernels communicate with ROS 2 using Zenoh‑pico for lightweight pub/sub, services, and actions over TCP, serial, or Ethernet, with zero‑copy CDR serialization and compile‑time buffer bounds. The CI pipeline integrates formal verification (Kani, CBMC) and WCET measurement, and a CLI generates Rust, C, and C++ bindings from ROS 2 interface definitions.

### The Caveats
The library’s claims are demonstrated only on QEMU simulations; there are no physical‑device benchmarks or baseline comparisons.

### Priority
The µRepRap micron‑scale printer offers the most concrete hardware breakthrough, immediately expanding fabrication capabilities for microrobotics and precision manufacturing.

### One action
Visit the µRepRap GitHub, download the design files for PIKA V0.02, and evaluate whether the 1 µm positioning claims meet your project’s precision needs.

### What to watch
Several items target manipulation advancement: P³‑WAM presents a unified perception‑prediction‑planning model, VaM focuses on online value‑guided policy improvement, and LIBERO‑PeRM provides a benchmark for preference‑aware manipulation. Together they signal a shift toward adaptable, instruction‑following robot hands, but each lacks thorough baselines or real‑world validation, so tracking future empirical studies will be key.
